text:
maria (PM): FYI — pulling together a compact priority index for customer-managed egress and VPC/on-prem packaging. I want a short list we can use for Q2 sprint planning. High level ask: which customer asks unblock deals vs. which are nice-to-have.

aditya (eng): Love this. Quick taxonomy idea: P1 = blocking (sales/legal), P2 = ops friction (manual cutover/work), P3 = UX/observability.

liz (solutions): Adding context from field: ACME & Nimbus require stable egress IPs and ability to bring their own NAT/VPN. They won't sign without egress pinning.

sophie (network PM): Proposed acceptance criteria for P1 (customer-managed egress):
- Installer supports --egress-mode=customer-managed (BYO NAT/NAT64 allowed)
- Deterministic egress CIDR mapping documented + test harness
- Rollback path: automatic revert of egress pin within 30m if canary fails
- Telemetry: we must emit egress-binding events to control-plane logs

aditya (eng): Implementation sketch for installer flags (for discussion):
```bash
./redwood-installer \
  --mode=onprem \
  --egress-mode=customer-managed \
  --egress-cidr=10.8.0.0/22 \
  --pin-model-versions=true \
  --edge-probe=true
```
We can wire the --egress-mode to the operator to apply a Kubernetes egressPolicy CR that maps service CIDRs to provided NAT IPs.

liz (solutions): Field notes: customers want both static IPs and a graceful handover window for upgrades. That suggests we need an egress-grace-period and a canary lane.

sophie (network PM): Suggest we surface three knobs in the Console: "egress mode", "canary cohort size", "egress-grace-period". Default: platform-managed, opt-in to customer-managed.

aditya (eng): Perf/effort notes: customer-managed egress is medium complexity. Big work items: operator CRD + validation, docs + tests, rollout canary automation. Estimate: 2 eng sprints to have a safe MVP (canary + rollback).

maria (PM): Prioritization vote: please react with :one:, :two:, :three: to map to P1/P2/P3 for your team. We need to finalize for the planning doc by EOD Fri.

ops-bot: Reminder: weekly release window Thursday 22:00–02:00 UTC. Any migration requiring egress handover must be scheduled outside that window.

aditya (eng): Quick edge-case: customers behind symmetric NAT still need outbound IP preservation. We'll need a compatibility test that simulates symmetric NAT and validates L7 connectivity.

liz (solutions): Customer-facing acceptance checklist (draft):
- preflight check passes with "egress-binding: OK"
- documented fallback (platform-managed) + consent flow
- runbook snippet for NetOps "re-home egress"

sophie (network PM): Launch gating criteria proposal for a P1 ship:
1) 3 enterprise customers complete on-prem canary with zero app-level failures for 48h
2) rollback tested and <30m recovery on two independent failure modes
3) public docs + runbook + 2 solution-engineer shadow sessions

aditya (eng): For upgrade paths: plan A = in-place rollover (dual-eip for X minutes), plan B = staged re-attach via routing change. We should include a sample flow in the operator code comments.

liz (solutions): Sample rollback command for runbook:
```bash
# revert egress pin for tenant-123
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: infra.redwood/v1
kind: EgressBinding
metadata:
  name: tenant-123
spec:
  mode: platform-managed
EOF
```
(we'll include a validated snippet in docs)

maria (PM): Risks called out: legal & procurement delays for customer-provided IPs, more complex support surface, and potential cost regressions for dual-eip canaries. Need SRE & support signoff.

aditya (eng): Next steps from eng side: spin up PR with CRD + minimal controller, integration test that verifies egress-binding event emitted, and a canary runner that toggles cohort size.

sophie (network PM): I'll own the gating checklist and coordinate shadow sessions. I'll add "NetOps preflight playbook" to the ship checklist.

maria (PM): OK — I'll synthesize into a short planning doc (will post link). For now: P1 candidates = ACME, Nimbus; P2 = smaller pilots that requested BYO VPN; P3 = UX polish requests.

deploy-bot: Meeting scheduled: "Egress priority sync" Thu 15:00 UTC — invite sent to participants.

liz (solutions): Quick ask — can we add a small telemetry field to the /status endpoint: "egress_mode": "customer-managed" so customer-run checks can see the current mode?

aditya (eng): Yes, that's trivial. We'll add egress_mode to the status API in the same PR.

maria (PM): Excellent. If no objections, I'll lock this down and add to the sprint planning doc. Please drop final blockers here before EOD. :thumbsup:
